To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cancer cells can polarize macrophages in vitro.
tumor-derived secreted molecules can influence macrophage polarization and function, and that the impact on macrophage polarization is cell type-specific and dependent on the microenvironment.
cancer cells influence macro-phage phenotype and function by secreting molecules that can be captured in conditioned medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cancer cells influence the immune response in the tumor environment, and how the tumor environment influences cancer progression.
the role of macrophages during the initiation and progression of cancer.
the molecular crosstalk between immune cells and cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these assays can be utilized to study cancer cell-induced polarization and activation of macrophages, and that they provide a valuable tool to study the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer-induced polarization of macro-phages.
the presented in vitro assays provide a powerful tool for the identification of the mechanisms by which cancer cell-derived factors influence macrophage polarization.
the presented protocols can be used to study the impact that cancer cells have on macrophages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer cells influence macro- phage polarization by inducing macrophages to acquire a pro- tumor phenotype.
cancer cells induce a pro-tumorigenic phenotype in macrophages.
cancer cells can influence the function of macrophages by secreting soluble molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer cells have the ability to polarize macrophages towards a pro-tumor phenotype, and that this polarization is mediated by secreted factors.
the polarization of macrophage populations in the tumor microenvironment is not only determined by the tumor itself but also by the tumor microenvironment.
cancer cells can polarize macrophages towards a pro-tumor phenotype by inducing expression of the pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage marker iNOS and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
